name: CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories (CSIR-NAL)

what_it_is.prose: CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories (CSIR-NAL) is India's premier civil-aerospace research and development laboratory, a constituent of the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research established in 1959 (originally the National Aeronautical Laboratory) and headquartered in Bengaluru. NAL's mandate spans indigenous civil aircraft design, aerospace composites, wind-tunnel and structural testing, and aeronautical technologies that also feed India's military-aircraft ecosystem. Its two flagship aircraft programmes are the HANSA-3 (NG) — a two-seat, all-composite trainer for private and commercial pilot licensing whose production version was launched on 29 November 2025 by Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh at the CSIR-NAL campus — and the SARAS Mk-2, a 19-seater pressurised light transport aircraft being developed for both civil regional connectivity and military operations, with features including a glass cockpit, digital avionics, autopilot and command-by-wire flight controls. HANSA-3 (NG) production has been transferred to industry partner M/s Pioneer Clean Amps, which is setting up a ₹150 crore facility at Kuppam, Andhra Pradesh, with capacity for about 100 aircraft a year, addressing a projected national need of nearly 30,000 pilots over 15-20 years. Alongside these aircraft, in November 2025 NAL inaugurated a SARAS Mk-2 Iron Bird full-system integration facility and a High Altitude Platforms (HAPS) solar-powered unmanned-aircraft fabrication facility, and formalised collaboration with Solar Defence & Aerospace Ltd. for a 150-kg-class loitering-munition UAV. NAL's wind tunnels, composite airframe technologies and structural-test capability are national assets used across defence aerospace programmes, giving it military-aerospace relevance beyond its civil aircraft.

deployments_procurement.summary: NAL is an R&D laboratory rather than a procurement contractor; its 'deployments' are aircraft programmes and national test infrastructure. The most significant recent milestone is the November 2025 launch of the production-standard HANSA-3 (NG) trainer with technology transfer to a private manufacturing partner, alongside the SARAS Mk-2 19-seater programme (dual civil/military use) and new HAPS and loitering-munition initiatives.

import_dependencies.summary: NAL's design, composites and testing work is indigenous, but its aircraft rely on imported propulsion and some avionics. The HANSA-3 (NG) uses an imported (Rotax-class) piston engine, and the SARAS Mk-2 integrates turboprop engines and avionics with foreign content. NAL's structural-test and wind-tunnel capability is domestic and a national strength.

faq.question: What is CSIR-NAL and what does it do?
faq.answer: CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories is India's premier civil-aerospace R&D laboratory, a constituent of the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research established in 1959 and based in Bengaluru. It designs indigenous civil aircraft (HANSA trainers and the SARAS light transport), develops aerospace composites, and operates national wind-tunnel, structural-test and flight-simulation facilities that also support India's military-aircraft programmes.

faq.question: What is the HANSA-3 (NG) and when did it enter production?
faq.answer: HANSA-3 (NG) is a two-seat, all-composite pilot trainer designed by CSIR-NAL for private and commercial pilot licensing. Its production version was launched on 29 November 2025 by Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh at the CSIR-NAL campus in Bengaluru. Production has been transferred to industry partner M/s Pioneer Clean Amps, which is establishing a ₹150 crore facility at Kuppam, Andhra Pradesh, capable of building up to 100 aircraft a year — aimed at India's projected need for nearly 30,000 pilots over the next 15-20 years.

faq.question: What is the SARAS Mk-2 and does it have a military role?
faq.answer: SARAS Mk-2 is a 19-seater pressurised light transport aircraft being developed by CSIR-NAL for both civil regional connectivity and military operations, with a glass cockpit, digital avionics, autopilot and command-by-wire flight controls. Its Iron Bird full-system integration facility was inaugurated in November 2025. NAL also inaugurated a High Altitude Platforms (HAPS) fabrication facility and formalised a collaboration for a 150-kg-class loitering-munition UAV, extending its relevance into military aerospace.
